asks.text: The art fetch couldn't bring the backgrounds folder Approved/Companion-Theme-Backdrops-P1-Complete12-v04 (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/14IhQiRJSyVKuoE3Ji2Rvo1Xi3i8GzAz-), because at 66 MB it went over the 100 MB limit together with the other art. So its 12 pictures…

Five Commons still need see-through pictures: Reedwatch Tinker, Millward Bellkeeper, Dewfern, Coppice Cricket and Unstitch. I suggest making each one the way you made Brickwarden, one character per picture on a see-through background, and approving each one before it goes in…

The game's companion pictures are 512×512, but the ten approved see-through pictures are bigger (1312×1199 or 1254×1254). Is it OK to make a smaller copy of each for the game, without changing anything else in it? I suggest yes. The approved originals would stay untouched in…

Each new Common needs one of the four summon bands. The Aberration, Unstitch, goes in the rarest band, and the other 14 go in groups of 5, 5 and 4. I suggest the first ten you approved fill the two groups of 5, and the last 4 fill the group of 4. Tell me if you'd rather pick…

Do you approve the ten plain dock card backgrounds (Dock-Card-Rarity-Skins-v01)? I suggest approving the colors and the plain middle, and letting the game draw the thin frame and edge marks itself, using your pictures as the guide. That keeps them sharp on a phone.

For the big companion screen, which companion gets which of the 12 scenes? I suggest matching each one to where it lives, for example wetlands for water beasts, and deciding that when the big screen is built.
Fungal Hollow's background has lettering in the lower left. I suggest making a clean new version without the lettering and putting it in its own new folder in your Artwork Inbox's Approved folder.

Moonlit Grove's background has dark bands across the top and bottom, and Lantern Gloom's has fainter ones. Should they be drawn again without the bands? I suggest yes for Moonlit Grove, and keeping Lantern Gloom until it's seen on the big screen.
